l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Elijah brought down kings (to destruction)
q: You brought down kings to destruction, and honorable men from their sickbeds.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Elijah heard rebuke at Sinai
q: You heard rebuke in Sinai, and judgments of vengeance in Horeb.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Elijah anointed kings (for retribution)
q: You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets to succeed after you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: You were taken up in a tempest of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: The memory of Josiah is like the composition of incense prepared by the work of the perfumer.

q: Ezekiel saw the vision of glory, which God showed him on the chariot of the cherubim.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: He comforted the people of Jacob, and delivered them by confident hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He was like a signet ring on the right hand.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jesus the son of Josedek built house (built by Jesus the son of Josedek)
q: So was Jesus the son of Josedek, who in their days built the house

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jesus the son of Josedek exalted a holy people (prepared for everlasting glory)

q: He raised up for us fallen walls, set up the gates and bars, and rebuilt our houses.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Nehemiah has memory great
q: Also of Nehemiah the memory is great.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Enoch was taken up from earth (unlike any man created)
q: No man was created upon the earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Josiah reformed the people (did what was right)
q: He did what was right in the reforming of the people, and took away the abominations of iniquity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Josiah set heart toward Lord (set right)
q: He set his heart right toward the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Josiah made prevail godliness (in lawless days)
q: In lawless days, he made godliness prevail.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: kings of Judah abandoned law of the Most High (all except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah)
q: Except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all were wicked, because they abandoned the law of the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: kings of Judah gave glory to foreign nation
q: They gave their power to others, and their glory to a foreign nation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: kings of Judah is wicked (except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah)
q: Except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all were wicked

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jeremiah was sanctified as prophet (sanctified in the womb)
q: he was sanctified in the womb to be a prophet, to root out, to afflict, to destroy and likewise to build and to plant.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Simon, the son of Onias is a high priest
q: It was Simon, the son of Onias, the high priest, who in his life repaired the house, and in his days strengthened the temple.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: book of instruction (Jesus's book) contains instruction of understanding and knowledge
q: I have written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is a King of all

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord guides him who does these things (the light of the Lord is his guide)
q: for the light of the Lord is his guide.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Simon, the son of Onias son of Onias
q: It was Simon, the son of Onias, the high priest

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Simon, the son of Onias strengthened house for God's name (Solomon's temple) (repaired the house)

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: He planned to save his people from ruin, and fortified the city against siege.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Simon, the son of Onias has kindred priests (Simon's kindred) (surrounding him like a garland at the altar)

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar is from Jerusalem
q: I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar authors book of instruction (Jesus's book)
q: I have written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar

s: the Lord takes vengeance on reader (addressee) (certain, if the reader presumes no one has dominion over him)
q: Don’t say, “Who will have dominion over me?” for the Lord will surely take vengeance on you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer is a disreputable title to avoid
q: Don’t be called a whisperer.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is patient
q: for the Lord is patient

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: A man’s tongue may be his downfall.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: Be steadfast in your understanding. Let your speech be consistent.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is a king
q: I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, and will praise you, O God my Savior.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) has possession tongue (given by the Lord as reward)
q: The Lord gave me a tongue for my reward.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) has heart joined with wisdom (from the beginning)
q: I got myself a heart joined with her from the beginning.

s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) was slandered to king (by an unrighteous tongue)
q: the slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: “Get her for yourselves without money.”

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is located near to find
q: She is near to find.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: I will give glory to him who gives me wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slanderous tongue is described as unrighteous (slandered the speaker to the king)
q: the slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slanderous tongue is described as unclean
q: from an unclean tongue, and from lying words—

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: uneducated (those invited to learn) is invited to house of instruction (speaker calls them to live there)
q: Draw near to me, all you who are uneducated, and live in the house of instruction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: uneducated (those invited to learn) has state thirsty souls (lacking in these things)
q: Why therefore are you all lacking in these things, and your souls are very thirsty?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is a savior of the speaker (addressed as God my Savior)
q: I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, and will praise you, O God my Savior.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: affliction (speaker's deliverance from death) is a many afflictions endured by the speaker (from which the Lord delivered him)
q: out of the many afflictions I endured,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord protects speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) (protector and helper)
q: for you have been my protector and helper, and delivered my body out of destruction,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord delivers those who wait for him (from the hand of their enemies)
q: how you deliver those who wait for you, and save them out of the hand of their enemies.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord has working from everlasting (his working)
q: your working which has been from everlasting

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord is father of speaker's Lord (the speaker calls on the Father of my Lord)
q: I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) seeks wisdom (sought openly in prayer while young; will seek to the end)
q: When I was yet young, before I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.

s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) has conduct uprightness (followed wisdom's steps from youth)
q: My foot walked in uprightness. From my youth I followed her steps.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (narrator of Chapter 51) has possession good possession (gained by seeking wisdom)
q: Therefore I have gained a good possession.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: A faithful friend is a strong defense.

q: And there is a friend who turns into an enemy. He will discover strife to your reproach.

q: If you are brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: And there is a friend who is a companion at the table, but he won’t continue in the day of your affliction.

s: Wisdom is harsh to unlearned person
q: How exceedingly harsh she is to the unlearned!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: For wisdom is according to her name. She isn’t manifest to many.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: She will rest upon him as a mighty stone of trial.

q: For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bands are a purple cord.

q: Even when you have gray hair you will find wisdom.

q: He who has found him has found a treasure.

q: My son, gather instruction from your youth up.

q: Stand in the multitude of the elders. Attach yourself to whomever is wise.

q: Let your mind dwell on the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually on his commandments.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord establishes heart of the one who meditates on his commandments (and grants desire for wisdom)
q: He will establish your heart and your desire for wisdom will be given to you.

q: for an evil name will inherit shame and reproach. So it is with the sinner who has a double tongue.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: There is nothing that can be taken in exchange for a faithful friend. His excellency is beyond price.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: faithful friend is a life-saving medicine
q: A faithful friend is a life-saving medicine.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: faithful friend is found by the Lord (those who fear the Lord find him)
q: Those who fear the Lord will find him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: He who fears the Lord directs his friendship properly; for as he is, so is his neighbor also.

q: If you want to gain a friend, get him in a time of testing, and don’t be in a hurry to trust him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus

q: Sweet words will multiply a man’s friends.

s: false friend lasts only for an occasion (does not continue in the day of affliction)
q: For there is a friend just for an occasion. He won’t continue in the day of your affliction.

q: Don’t hate hard labor or farm work, which the Most High has created.

q: My son, don’t sow upon the furrows of unrighteousness, and you won’t reap them sevenfold.

q: Don’t neglect to give alms.

s: almsgiving and charity completes blessing (stretching out a hand to the poor man)
q: Also stretch out your hand to the poor man, that your blessing may be complete.

q: Let your soul love a wise servant. Don’t defraud him of liberty.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord humbles and exalts men (in the bitterness of their souls)
q: for there is one who humbles and exalts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is called the Most High
q: Don’t hate hard labor or farm work, which the Most High has created.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is creator of humankind (the one to be loved with all one's strength)
q: With all your strength love him who made you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord receives fear and love (commanded of the reader, with all soul and strength)
q: Fear the Lord with all your soul; and revere his priests.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: priests are owed first fruits and holy portions (as commanded)
q: Fear the Lord and honor the priest. Give him his portion, even as it is commanded you: the first fruits, the trespass offering, the gift of the shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of holy things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: priests are to be revered (as ministers of the Lord)
q: Fear the Lord with all your soul; and revere his priests.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: priests are not to be forsaken as his ministers (love him who made you with all your strength)
q: With all your strength love him who made you. Don’t forsake his ministers.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: evil and unrighteousness results in punishment (evil overtakes those who do it; unrighteousness yields sevenfold reaping)
q: Do no evil, so no evil will overtake you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mighty man is warned against contending with him (risk of falling into his hands)
q: Don’t contend with a mighty man, lest perhaps you fall into his hands.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the wise teaches discipline (through their proverbs)
q: for from them you will learn discipline and how to serve great men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man has disposition overpowers those who strive with him (risk when striven with)
q: Don’t strive with a rich man, lest perhaps he overpower you

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sons of Adam is warned against opening one's heart to him
q: Don’t open your heart to every man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: death applies to all
q: Remember that we all die.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: practical wisdom and prudent conduct toward others advises avoiding conflict with the powerful
q: Don’t contend with a mighty man, lest perhaps you fall into his hands.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: riches has effect destroys many
q: for gold has destroyed many, and turned away the hearts of kings.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: riches affects kings (turns away their hearts)
q: for gold has destroyed many, and turned away the hearts of kings.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the wise has possession discourse and proverbs (source of discipline and how to serve great men)
q: Don’t neglect the discourse of the wise. Be conversant with their proverbs; for from them you will learn discipline and how to serve great men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: woman has effect leads many astray by her beauty (passion kindled like a fire)
q: Many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman; and with this, passion is kindled like a fire.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: choosing good companions recommends men of understanding (conversation partners)
q: Let your conversation be with men of understanding.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: choosing good companions recommends righteous people (companions at the table)
q: Let righteous people be companions at your table.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: choosing good companions recommends wise (take counsel with them)
q: take counsel with the wise.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: choosing good companions recommends neighbors (aim to know them)
q: aim to know your neighbors

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: avoiding sexual temptation from women advises turning your eye away from a beautiful woman
q: Turn your eye away from a beautiful woman, and don’t gaze at another’s beauty.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: avoiding sexual temptation from women advises not dining with a woman who has a husband (lest your soul turn to her)
q: Don’t dine at all with a woman who has a husband, or revel with her at wine, lest perhaps your soul turn away to her, and with your spirit you slide into destruction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: old friend is not comparable to new friend (should not be forsaken)
q: Don’t forsake an old friend; for a new one is not comparable to him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord holds in hand government of the earth
q: The government of the earth is in the Lord’s hand.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: pride is not created for men
q: Pride has not been created for men, nor wrathful anger for the offspring of women.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: nations undergo transfer of sovereignty (because of injustice, violence, and greed for money)
q: Sovereignty is transferred from nation to nation because of injustice, violence, and greed for money.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: judge influences officials (as is the judge, so are his officials)
q: As is the judge of his people, so are his officials.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: judge is when wise instructs his people (wise judge)
q: A wise judge will instruct his people.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: king destroys when undisciplined people (undisciplined king)
q: An undisciplined king will destroy his people.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: king is subject to death (the king of today will die tomorrow)
q: The king of today will die tomorrow.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord have honor (in the Lord's eyes)
q: Those who fear the Lord have honor in his eyes.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord are greater than prince, judge, and mighty man
q: There is not one of them greater than he who fears the Lord.
